designs.title: Belize
designs.why: The engraving is strong and holds up in one ink: palms stepping down to the hut, a jetty that leads the eye in from the right, coral that breaks up the water, and the solid blacks print cleanly at full size. The type lockup is the weak part. BELIZE and its rule sit about 650 px (roughly 5.5 cm) above the palm tops, so on the tee the heading floats off as a separate label instead of capping the scene. The heading is a slab typewriter face but the coordinates are a geometric grotesk, two voices that don't match. The coordinates are set small and sit tight under the coral while the space above is wasted. The scene is also lopsided: the jetty is cut hard at the right edge while the left fades out into scattered coral.
designs.fix: Close the dead band: move BELIZE and its rule down to about 150-200 px above the tallest palm (or scale the scene up into that space), so heading, scene and coordinates read as one tight centred block. Then set the coordinates in the heading's slab face, tracked to the width of the rule.
